description: Incremental upgrade path to modernize the repo. Each phase is designed to be mergeable independently to limit blast radius. Phases carry a `depends_on` list; anything not in that list can ship in any order relative to it. Targets were re-planned on 2026-10-23 against version_dates/latest_versions.json (generated by version_dates/fetch_latest_versions.py). Phases 1–5 are history and kept verbatim for the tracking files that reference them. Statuses and the Track B detail (Phases 11–12) were refreshed on 2026-10-25 with Track A merged (Phases 6–9) and Phase 10 green in CI; see status_2026_10_25.

ordering_constraints: Rails 7.1 and 7.2 run on Ruby 3.1; Rails 8.0 and 8.1 require Ruby >= 3.2. So the two 7.x Rails steps come before the Ruby bump and the two 8.x steps come after it.
The official ruby image has no 3.1 Trixie tag (3.1 is EOL), so Debian Trixie requires the Ruby bump first.
Rails 7.2 is tested on Ruby 3.4 but not on Ruby 4.0; Ruby 4.0 fixes landed in Rails 8.0.4.1+/8.1.3+. So Ruby goes 3.1 → 3.4 before the Rails 8 steps and 3.4 → 4.0 after Rails 8.1.

Devise 5 (Rails >= 7.0), puma 8 (Ruby >= 3.0), pg 1.7 (Ruby >= 3.1), jwt 3, dartsass-sprockets (Ruby >= 3.1) and the Node bump have no Rails or Ruby prerequisite beyond what main already has — they can all start now and ship in parallel with the Rails 7.x steps.

haml 7, nokogiri 1.19, bundler 4, web-console 4.3, faker 3.8 and zeitwerk 2.8 need Ruby >= 3.2; selenium-webdriver 4.51, shoulda-matchers 8 and simplecov 1.x need Ruby >= 3.3. They ride with or after the Ruby 3.4 phase.
Rails.application.secrets is deprecated in 7.1 and removed in 7.2; config.read_encrypted_secrets (set in production.rb) is removed in 8.0. Both go in the Rails 7.1 phase.

config.load_defaults climbs one version per Rails phase, always to the version that is already running in production, so a defaults flip is never in the same PR as the framework bump that introduced it.

phases.name: Rails 5.2 → 6.1
phases.rationale: Rails 6.1 is the last major version that still supports Ruby 2.7, making it the safest first step. Skipping 6.0 is intentional — 6.1 has better LTS-era gem support and a more complete upgrade guide.
known_risks: Zeitwerk autoloader replaces classic autoloader — requires all files to follow naming conventions exactly
Action Mailer, ActiveRecord, and ActiveStorage APIs have deprecation removals between 5.2 and 6.1
sprockets 4 changes manifest.js format — assets:precompile behavior changes

phases.name: Ruby 2.7.7 → 3.1.x + replace therubyracer
phases.rationale: Ruby 3.0 made keyword argument separation mandatory (no longer a warning). Ruby 3.1 is the minimum for the subsequent Rails upgrade. This phase also drops therubyracer, which does not build reliably on Ruby 3.x, replacing it with mini_racer.
known_risks: therubyracer removal can break asset compilation if mini_racer is not added — test assets:precompile explicitly
Ruby 3.0 keyword argument changes (hash-as-kwargs) can cause ArgumentError in app and gem code — run full test suite and watch for failures
coffee-rails still works but CoffeeScript is end-of-life; no urgent action required yet

phases.name: Linux Bullseye → Bookworm (OpenSSL 1.1.1 → 3.0)
phases.rationale: Debian Bookworm (12) ships with OpenSSL 3.0, which is actively maintained. OpenSSL 1.1.1 reached end-of-life in September 2023. Separating the OS bump from Ruby/Rails upgrades makes it easy to bisect if anything breaks.
known_risks: OpenSSL 3.0 deprecates legacy cryptographic algorithms — if any OAuth or JWT configuration uses weak algorithms (MD5, RC4, etc.) it will fail
System library package names occasionally differ between Bullseye and Bookworm — verify apt-get install lines in all Dockerfiles still resolve

phases.name: omniauth 1 → 2
phases.rationale: omniauth 2.x drops GET-based OAuth authorize requests (CSRF fix) and, with Rails/Devise, requires the omniauth-rails_csrf_protection adapter. Shipping it separately from the Rails bump keeps an OAuth regression attributable to this change alone — it is the highest-risk piece of the path, so it ships and gets verified on staging by itself.
known_risks: omniauth 2.x rejects GET /auth/:provider — the sign-in links must become POST buttons (button_to) carrying the Rails authenticity token
The smoke suite can only cover the authorize redirect, not the provider callback — verify Google and GitHub sign-in manually on staging before promoting

phases.name: Rails 6.1 → 7.0
phases.rationale: First of three Rails steps (7.0 → 7.1 → 7.2), all on Ruby 3.1. Rails 7.0 removes APIs deprecated during the 6.x cycle; taking it as its own phase keeps the removal fallout separate from the 7.1 and 7.2 behavior changes. Spring 2.x pins spring < 3.0 via spring-watcher-listen and does not load under Rails 7 — it is removed rather than upgraded since nobody runs Spring inside Docker.

changes.spring: remove spring + spring-watcher-listen (spring 2 is pinned < 3.0 and does not load under Rails 7)
changes.new_framework_defaults: add config/initializers/new_framework_defaults_7_0.rb with every default commented out
changes.load_defaults: stays 6.1 — bumping to 7.0 (cookie serializer, cache format, button_to behavior, etc.) is a deliberate follow-up after this phase is on production

known_risks: Rails 7.0 removes ActiveRecord, ActionView, and ActiveSupport APIs deprecated in 6.x — run the full suite and grep for DEPRECATION warnings to build the 7.1 to-do list
sprockets 4 + sass-rails/sassc-rails are retained (no dartsass-rails migration in this phase); sassc is unmaintained but still builds on Ruby 3.1
turbolinks 5 is retained; the Hotwire/Turbo migration is out of scope

phases.name: Node 20 → 26 LTS + CI compose cleanup
phases.shipped: squash 935e2cb merged 2026-10-24; image 0.9.6-901; base image 0.8.0 published multi-arch; in production since 2026-10-25 (core-iac #342). Also removed yarn from all images (see phase_6_tracking.json)
phases.rationale: Node 20 went end-of-life on 2026-04-30 and receives no security patches; it is installed in every image (base, development, production) purely as the ExecJS runtime for CoffeeScript and uglifier. Node 26 enters Active LTS on 2026-10-28 (EOL 2029-04-30). Node 24 (Maintenance LTS from 2026-10-20, EOL 2028-04-30) is the fallback if the NodeSource 26.x channel does not yet publish Bookworm packages. The CircleCI job also downloads docker-compose 1.18.0 (2018, compose v1) even though every ./go script already calls the `docker compose` v2 plugin that ships in cimg images — delete the download.

changes.nodesource: setup_20.x → setup_26.x in Dockerfile.base, Dockerfile.development, Dockerfile.production (setup_24.x if 26 is not packaged for Bookworm)
changes.yarn: keep `npm install -g yarn` (nothing in the repo uses yarn or node_modules at runtime — consider dropping in the same PR)
changes.circleci: remove the docker-compose 1.18.0 curl/mv step and COMPOSE_TLS_VERSION; keep setup_remote_docker
changes.base_image_version: 0.7.0 → 0.8.0 (rebuilt with Node 26); bump scripts/docker_hub.rb BASE_VERSION, scripts/docker_build.rb and Dockerfile.ci

known_risks: ExecJS picks Node automatically; a Node major bump only matters if uglifier/coffee-script output changes — assets:precompile runs in Dockerfile.production so CI covers it
NodeSource channel availability per Debian release is not announced in advance — the Dockerfile build will fail fast if the apt repo is missing

phases.name: puma 5 → 8 + pg 1.5 → 1.7
phases.shipped: squash fea6299 merged 2026-10-25; image 0.9.6-906; staging and production via core-iac #345 the same day, smoke 49/0/2 before and after on both. pg installs as a precompiled gem with bundled libpq 18.6, so the image's libpq-dev is only a source-build fallback now (see phase_7_tracking.json)
phases.rationale: Both are runtime gems with no Rails-version coupling that are three and two majors behind. puma 8.0.2 (2026-05-26) supports Ruby >= 3.0; pg 1.7.0 (2026-10-02) supports Ruby >= 3.1 and < 4.1 and is the version that will be carried through the Ruby 4.0 step. Shipping them together, ahead of any Rails step, keeps a server-level regression (threads, bind, graceful restart, DB reconnect) attributable to this pair.

changes.config_puma_rb: re-review against the Rails 7.0 template; the current file only sets threads/port/environment/tmp_restart

known_risks: puma 6 changed the default `wait_for_less_busy_worker` and request-queue behaviour, puma 7 dropped Ruby < 3.0 and renamed some env vars — read the 6.0, 7.0 and 8.0 upgrade notes; the app runs single-process (no `workers`) so cluster-mode changes should not apply
pg 1.6+ ships precompiled native gems per platform; the lockfile must keep `aarch64-linux`, `ruby` and `x86_64-linux` in PLATFORMS (local arm64 vs CI x86_64)
The /health endpoint's DB connection check and the smoke suite exercise pg end-to-end on staging

phases.name: Devise 4.9 → 5.0 + jwt 2 → 3 + OmniAuth adapter bumps
phases.shipped: squash 6c947b8 merged 2026-10-25; image 0.9.6-908; staging and production via core-iac #346 the same day, smoke 49/0/2 before and after on both; full GitHub and Google sign-in round trips verified on production. Devise.secret_key unchanged in every environment, so no token invalidation (see phase_8_tracking.json)
phases.rationale: Everything that touches authentication, in one reviewable PR, verified on staging the same way Phase 4 was. Devise 5.0 (2026-01-23, 5.0.4 is current) requires Rails >= 7.0 and Ruby >= 2.7, so it works on main today; its only hard removal that affected this app (devise_error_messages!) was already handled in PR #217. jwt 3.x (3.0.0 2025-06-14, 3.3.0 2026-09-11) changes verification and error classes; JwtTokenService uses plain HS256 encode/decode with a string secret, which is unchanged, and rescues JWT::ExpiredSignature / JWT::DecodeError, which still exist. omniauth-rails_csrf_protection 2.0.1 and omniauth-google-oauth2 1.2.3 are patch-level follow-ups to Phase 4.
known_risks: Devise 5: `Devise.secret_key` now defaults to `Rails.application.secret_key_base`; if the value differs from what SecretKeyFinder resolved under 4.9, outstanding password-reset / confirmation tokens become invalid (sessions are unaffected). In production both read ENV['SECRET_KEY_BASE'], so expect no change — confirm on staging.

Devise 5: generated views changed (`

` wrappers instead of `
`, new reset-password button label, `[data-turbo-temporary]`); the app has copied views under app/views/devise so nothing changes automatically — diff against the new generator output and adopt deliberately
Devise 5: `sign_in(resource, scope)` positional scope and `Devise::TestHelpers` are removed — grep spec/ for both before bumping
Devise 5: the OmniAuth route now derives its verbs from `OmniAuth.config.allowed_request_methods` — matches the POST-only setup from Phase 4

jwt 3: Base64 decoding is strict (RFC 4648); a token with whitespace or a trailing newline now raises instead of decoding. API clients that pass tokens from files could regress — the smoke suite's visitor flow covers the normal path

jwt 3.3: errors were reorganised under JWT::Error; signing failures raise JWT::EncodeError instead of DecodeError/ArgumentError. JwtTokenService only rescues on decode, so no change is needed, but spec/services/jwt_token_service_spec.rb should assert the round trip explicitly
As in Phase 4, the smoke suite covers only the authorize redirect — manual Google and GitHub sign-in on staging before promoting

phases.name: sassc-rails → dartsass-sprockets (+ uglifier → terser)
phases.shipped: squash 26acbeb merged 2026-10-25; image 0.9.6-909; core-iac #347 bumped all three environments; staging verified (smoke 49/0/2, asset check: application.css 158 KB now with a UTF-8 BOM, application.js 2.65 MB via terser); production apply pending confirmation when this was written. The predicted slash-division warnings never appeared (bootstrap 4.6.2 uses divide()); 307 of 312 Dart Sass warnings come from Bootstrap and are hidden by quiet_deps (see phase_9_tracking.json)
phases.rationale: sassc 2.4.0 (2020) wraps the end-of-life libsass and compiles ~30 MB of C++ during every `bundle install`; it is the single slowest step in the base image build and the component most likely to stop building on Ruby 4.0. dartsass-sprockets 3.2.1 (Ruby >= 3.1) is a drop-in replacement for sassc-rails on the existing Sprockets pipeline, backed by the maintained sass-embedded gem (Dart Sass). uglifier 4.2.1 still works (with `harmony: true` from Phase 5) but terser 1.2.8 is the maintained JS compressor and understands modern syntax natively. Doing this before the Ruby bumps means the Ruby phases do not also have to debug a native-extension build.

changes.uglifier: 4.1.11 → remove; add terser ~> 1.2 and set `config.assets.js_compressor = :terser` in production.rb
changes.dockerfiles: `gem install nokogiri -v …` pre-install lines stay; nothing else changes

known_risks: Dart Sass warns on `@import` and on `/` division; bootstrap 4.6's SCSS triggers the division warnings. They are warnings, not errors, but will be noisy in assets:precompile output until Bootstrap 5 (standing note)
Dart Sass is stricter about some libsass extensions (e.g. `!global` without prior declaration, unquoted strings in some functions) — the app's eight .scss files are small; precompile in CI catches it
Visual regression is the real risk: compare the landing page, scenario show page and auth pages on staging against production before promoting
terser output differs from uglifier's; the Plotly bundle and CoffeeScript output must still load — the chart page is the smoke check

phases.name: Dev/test tooling catch-up on Ruby 3.1
phases.shipped: draft PR #227, CI green (build 910) on a head that includes main through Phase 9. Landed versions differ slightly from the estimates below: faker 3.6.1 (not 3.5.x), selenium-webdriver 4.32.0, byebug 12.0.0 (13 needs Ruby 3.2), pry 0.16.1 — pry's move matters because 0.12.2 fails to load on Ruby >= 3.2 (PR #229 finding). rubocop: 56 new offences, 38 lines autocorrected, 3 cops scoped in .rubocop.yml, none inline. spec/rails_helper.rb now uses Rails.root.join('spec/fixtures').to_s for fixture_path (Phase 11 turns it into fixture_paths)
phases.rationale: Everything in the development/test groups that is several majors behind but still has a release supporting Ruby 3.1. Done as its own PR because it changes lint output and spec infrastructure, not app behaviour. rubocop 1.28 (2022) → 1.9x is the big one: `require:` becomes `plugins:` (rubocop 1.72+), rubocop-rspec 3 moved its Capybara and FactoryBot cops to rubocop-capybara / rubocop-factory_bot, and TargetRubyVersion 3.1 stays until the Ruby phase. annotate 3.2.0 (2022) is unmaintained and breaks on Rails 7.2+; annotaterb is the maintained fork and must be in place before Phase 12.

changes.rubocop: ~> 1.28.0 → ~> 1.92 (NewCops stays `disable`; fix or disable new offences in .rubocop.yml, not inline)
changes.annotate: 3.2.0 → remove; add annotaterb ~> 4.25 and run `annotaterb config:generate`
changes.database_cleaner: 1.7.0 → database_cleaner-active_record ~> 2.2 (the meta-gem split into adapters in 2.0)
changes.selenium_webdriver: 4.9.0 → newest 4.x that still allows Ruby 3.1 (4.51 requires 3.3 — rides with Phase 13); no spec is currently tagged `js: true`, so this gem is effectively unused

CI fails on any RuboCop offence, including scripts/ and config/ — run ./go lint before every push in this phase

annotaterb writes annotations in a slightly different format — expect a one-time diff across app/models and spec/factories

phases.name: Rails 7.0 → 7.1 (+ load_defaults 7.0, secrets → secret_key_base)
phases.rationale: Second Rails step on Ruby 3.1. Rails 7.1 deprecates Rails.application.secrets (removed in 7.2) and rspec-rails deprecates config.fixture_path (→ fixture_paths). With 7.0 on production since 0.9.6-871, this PR also flips config.load_defaults 6.1 → 7.0 and deletes new_framework_defaults_7_0.rb. Depends on Phase 10 only because annotate 3.2 and rubocop-rails 2.14 do not understand Rails 7.1+ and the lint job would fail. Detail below was worked out on 2026-10-25 against main at 26acbeb (Phase 9) plus PR #227; every file:line was grep-verified then.

changes.rspec_rails: ~> 6.0 → ~> 7.1 (7.1.1, 2025-02-06, is the last 7.x; 8.0.4 stays for Phase 15 as planned)
changes.load_defaults: config/application.rb: 6.1 → 7.0; delete config/initializers/new_framework_defaults_7_0.rb (every key in it is commented out today, so each 7.0 default below switches on in this PR); add new_framework_defaults_7_1.rb from `rails app:update` with everything commented out
changes.secrets: app/services/jwt_token_service.rb:26 `Rails.application.secrets.secret_key_base.to_s` → `Rails.application.secret_key_base`; delete config/secrets.yml (it only maps ENV['SECRET_KEY_BASE'] into secrets for all three environments); remove `config.read_encrypted_secrets = true` from config/environments/production.rb:21 (removed outright in 8.0)
changes.secret_key_base_in_dev_and_test: Rails 7.1's Application#secret_key_base ignores ENV['SECRET_KEY_BASE'] in development and test (it uses config.secret_key_base or generates tmp/local_secret.txt); today those environments get the compose SECRET_KEY_BASE through secrets.yml. Add `config.secret_key_base = ENV['SECRET_KEY_BASE']` to development.rb and test.rb so Rails, Devise (config/initializers/devise.rb:11 reads the ENV directly) and JwtTokenService keep sharing one secret locally. config/environments/test.rb:54 `config.secret_key = ENV['SECRET_KEY_BASE']` is not a Rails option (Railtie::Configuration#method_missing stores it, nothing reads it) — replace it with the secret_key_base line. Production is unaffected: ENV['SECRET_KEY_BASE'] is consulted first there
changes.fixture_path: spec/rails_helper.rb: `config.fixture_path = Rails.root.join('spec/fixtures').to_s` (as PR #227 leaves it) → `config.fixture_paths = [Rails.root.join('spec/fixtures')]`; no spec uses fixtures (FactoryBot throughout), so the line is kept only for rspec-rails' own expectations
changes.show_exceptions: config/environments/test.rb:31 `config.action_dispatch.show_exceptions = false` → `:none` (7.1 deprecates the booleans; :none is the exact equivalent of false)
changes.schema_rb: db/schema.rb still says `ActiveRecord::Schema[6.1]` (production has dump_schema_after_migration = false and the suite only loads it). Run `rails db:schema:dump` in the dev container after the bump and commit the `[7.1]` header; expect no column changes
changes.rails_app_update: run in a scratch copy and review hunk by hunk, as in Phase 5 (PR #215 documents what was accepted/rejected then — the same quote-style and production.rb rewrites will be rejected again). Expected 7.1 hunks and disposition: accept `config.autoload_lib(ignore: %w[assets tasks])` in application.rb (lib/allowed_hosts.rb is `require`d explicitly by config/initializers/host_authorization.rb; keep that require, autoload_lib is additive); accept `config.enable_reloading` in place of `config.cache_classes` in the three environment files (same semantics, inverted); accept the new :passw/:email/... keys in filter_parameter_logging.rb; reject `config.silence_healthcheck_path = '/up'` (the probe path is /health), the production.rb `config.active_support.report_deprecations = false` rewrite (keep `deprecation = :notify`), the public_file_server/assume_ssl/force_ssl rewrites, bin/* and .gitattributes, and the content_security_policy.rb / permissions_policy.rb rewrites (both files are all comments today, nothing to gain)
changes.turbolinks: optional, separate commit: 5.1.1 → 5.2.1 (standing note; the only turbolinks release since 2018)

load_defaults_7_0_effects_here.key_generator_hash_digest_class_sha256: THE decision in this phase. ActiveSupport::KeyGenerator switches from SHA1 to SHA256, so every key derived from secret_key_base changes: the encrypted session cookie can no longer be read, which signs out every user (no rememberable module, so sessions are all they have) and drops `session[:visitor_id]` (app/controllers/concerns/visitable.rb:11) — each anonymous visitor becomes a new Visitor row and loses the scenarios tied to the old one (the rows stay, orphaned). Devise's recoverable tokens derive from the same KeyGenerator, so password-reset emails sent before the deploy stop working (reset_password_within is 6 hours, acceptable). JWTs are NOT affected: JwtTokenService signs with secret_key_base directly, not through the KeyGenerator. Recommendation: ship the `config/initializers/cookie_rotator.rb` from the Rails 7.0 upgrade guide ('Key generator digest class changing to use SHA256') so SHA1-derived :encrypted and :signed cookies are still read and rewritten in the new format on the first request; remove the rotator in Phase 12 once Phase 11 has been on production for a while (the Devise session cookie has no expiry, so the tail is whatever is left by then). Alternative if the rotator misbehaves on staging: set `config.active_support.key_generator_hash_digest_class = OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1` right after load_defaults 7.0 and carry the decision to Phase 12
load_defaults_7_0_effects_here.hash_digest_class_sha256: changes ETags and cache keys only; the app has no fragment caching and no shared cache store (production uses the default :file_store in the pod's tmp/cache) — no effect
load_defaults_7_0_effects_here.cache_format_version_7_0: set automatically by load_defaults 7.0 (the 7.0 defaults file says to put it in application.rb, which load_defaults does); :null_store in test, :null_store/:memory_store in development, ephemeral :file_store in production — no shared cache to migrate
load_defaults_7_0_effects_here.button_to_generates_button_tag: app/views/devise/shared/_links.html.haml:24 passes the label as the first argument, so the OAuth sign-in control changes from <input type=submit value=…> to <button>…</button>. Same `btn btn-link` classes; Capybara's click_on finds both; spec/smoke/oauth_providers_spec.rb posts the form itself. Eyeball the sign-in page on staging
load_defaults_7_0_effects_here.raise_on_open_redirects: every redirect_to in app/controllers targets a path, a record or a same-host *_url (users/omniauth_callbacks_controller.rb:18 new_user_registration_url) — nothing external, no `allow_other_host:` needed
load_defaults_7_0_effects_here.default_headers: X-XSS-Protection becomes 0 and Referrer-Policy / X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies are added; the only header any spec asserts on is Access-Token (spec/requests/api/v1/*)
load_defaults_7_0_effects_here.partial_inserts_false: INSERTs list every column; the schema has plain defaults only (no expression defaults) — no behaviour change, verify with the suite
load_defaults_7_0_effects_here.executor_around_test_case: enables the Active Record query cache inside each example; the suite writes only through Active Record (factories), so stale reads are not expected — if a spec goes red only under this flag, that is the cause
load_defaults_7_0_effects_here.return_only_request_media_type_on_conten: no caller of request.content_type in app/
load_defaults_7_0_effects_here.remaining_keys: apply_stylesheet_media_default (layouts pass media: 'all' explicitly), remove_deprecated_time_with_zone_name, use_rfc4122_namespaced_uuids (Visitor uses SecureRandom, not Digest::UUID), verify_foreign_keys_for_fixtures (no fixtures), automatic_scope_inversing, action_mailer.smtp_timeout, every active_storage.* key (Active Storage unused) — no effect expected

phases.name: Ruby 3.1 → 3.4 (+ bundler 2.7, nokogiri 1.19, Ruby-gated test gems)
phases.rationale: Ruby 3.1 has been EOL since 2025-03-26. Ruby 3.4 (EOL 2028-03-31) is the right intermediate target: Rails 7.2 supports it and Rails 8.0/8.1 require >= 3.2. Ruby 4.0 is deliberately not taken here because Rails 7.2 is not tested on it. Going 3.1 → 3.4 in one step is fine for this codebase: the 3.2 (`rb_cData` C-API removal) and 3.3 changes are transparent to a pure-Ruby app with precompiled nokogiri/pg, and the 3.4 changes (frozen-string 'chilled' warnings, `it` block parameter, new Hash#inspect format) surface as warnings or spec diffs, not crashes. This is a Docker base image change, kept separate from the Rails steps so any regression is attributable to the runtime.

changes.bundler: 2.4.22 → 2.7.x (the bundler Ruby 3.4 ships; Bundler 4 waits for Ruby 4.0)
changes.nokogiri: 1.18.10 → 1.19.4 (1.19 requires Ruby >= 3.2); update the `gem install nokogiri -v` lines in all three Dockerfiles
changes.ruby_gated_gems: selenium-webdriver → 4.51, shoulda-matchers → 8.0, simplecov → 1.3, faker → 3.8, web-console → 4.3, byebug → 13, zeitwerk → 2.8 (all previously held back by Ruby 3.1)

Ruby 3.4 changed Hash#inspect to `{key: value}` / `{"k" => v}`; any spec asserting on inspected output (error messages included) will need updating

Ruby 3.3/3.4 moved base64, bigdecimal, csv, drb, mutex_m, nkf, syslog to bundled gems; the lockfile already carries base64, bigdecimal, drb and mutex_m via Rails 7.x, so expect at most a Gemfile line for csv if anything requires it
Local arm64 vs CI x86_64: `./go build` on a Mac produces the aarch64 base image; CI builds x86_64. Both must succeed before the base image version is tagged
The `ruby-dev` apt package in the Dockerfiles installs Debian's own Ruby headers, not the image's — it has been harmless so far but is pointless; drop it here or in Phase 14

phases.name: Linux Bookworm → Trixie (OpenSSL 3.0 → 3.5 LTS)
phases.rationale: Debian 12 Bookworm left regular security support on 2026-07-11 (LTS to 2028-06-30) and its OpenSSL 3.0 passed upstream EOL on 2026-09-07. Debian 13 Trixie (released 2025-08-09, security support to 2028-08-09, LTS to 2030-06-30) ships OpenSSL 3.5 LTS (EOL 2030-04-08). The official ruby image publishes slim-trixie tags for 3.2+ only, hence the dependency on Phase 13. Same shape as Phase 3: one FROM line change per Dockerfile, verified by bisecting separately from the Ruby bump.

changes.docker_base_image: ruby:3.4.12-slim-bookworm → ruby:3.4.12-slim-trixie in Dockerfile.base, Dockerfile.development, Dockerfile.production
changes.libpq: Bookworm's libpq-dev is PostgreSQL 15; Trixie's is 17 — pg 1.7 links against it at build time, no app change
changes.apt_packages: build-essential, patch, zlib1g-dev, liblzma-dev, libpq-dev, curl all keep their names; drop ruby-dev (see Phase 13)
changes.nodesource: setup_26.x publishes Trixie packages; no change expected from Phase 6

known_risks: OpenSSL 3.5 keeps the 3.0 provider model, so the Phase 3 legacy-algorithm check already covers it; TLS 1.3 to Google/GitHub OAuth endpoints and RDS is unaffected
Trixie uses the merged-/usr layout and `apt` 3.x; the Dockerfiles use plain `apt-get install -y` so nothing changes, but any future apt-key usage would break
Trixie's default `useradd` and `/etc/subuid` behaviour is unchanged for the `--uid` dev-user pattern in Dockerfile.development — ./go start with a bind-mounted tree is the local check

SPIKE (PR #229): Trixie ships GCC 14, which turns -Wincompatible-pointer-types into an error; any C extension still at a 2018-era release fails to compile (byebug 10 did). Run a per-gem `gem install` probe of every native gem in the lockfile before the image bump
SPIKE: with pg 1.6+/1.7 the precompiled gem bundles its own libpq and OpenSSL, so Trixie's libpq-dev is no longer what the app links against (Phase 7 already made this switch on Bookworm)

Propshaft becomes the default asset pipeline for *new* apps only; sprockets-rails 3.5.2 remains supported and stays. Flips load_defaults to 7.2.

phases.name: haml 5 → 7
phases.rationale: haml 5.2.2 (2021) predates Ruby 3.2 and is the gem most likely to break under Ruby 4.0's string and Set changes. haml 6 replaced the implementation with Hamlit (much faster) and removed every Haml helper except `preserve`; haml 7 (7.5.1 current, requires Ruby >= 3.2) changed the default attribute quote from ' to ". Done after the Ruby 3.4 bump and before the Ruby 4.0 bump so each regression is attributable.

phases.name: Ruby 3.4 → 4.0 (+ Bundler 4 / RubyGems 4)
phases.rationale: Ruby 4.0 (2025-12-25; 4.0.9 current, EOL 2029-03-31) is the final runtime target. It needs Rails 8.0.4.1+/8.1.3+ (Phase 16), haml 7 (Phase 17) and a Trixie image (Phase 14; ruby:4.0.x-slim-trixie exists, there is no Bookworm tag for 4.0). Ruby 4.0 ships RubyGems 4 and Bundler 4, which change lockfile defaults — that is the real content of this phase. The spike in PR #229 proved the mechanical part on today's main; this phase remains last only because Rails 7.x is unsupported on Ruby 4.0 and the toolchain (rubocop, base image) has to move first.

changes.bundler: 2.7.x → 4.0.x (Ruby 4.0.9 ships Bundler 4.0.20, not the newest 4.0.x): BUNDLED WITH keeps the full patch level and the lockfile gains NO CHECKSUMS section unless created fresh or with `--add-checksums`; Bundler 4 deprecates the Gemfile's `:mingw`/`:x64_mingw` platform symbols (drop them from the byebug line); multiple global `source` lines are rejected; `bundle install --binstubs` errors. Bundler also self-downgrades to the lockfile's BUNDLED WITH version inside the image until the lockfile is regenerated. Update the `gem install bundler -v` lines in all three Dockerfiles
changes.bundled_gems: ostruct, logger, benchmark, pstore, rdoc, irb are bundled gems in 4.0 — config 5.6.1 already depends on ostruct and Rails on logger, so no Gemfile change was needed in the spike; tsort becomes a bundled gem in 4.1 and railties 7.0 already warns about it
changes.pg: 1.7.0 declares `< 4.1.dev`, so it is fine; re-check nokogiri, byebug and web-console release notes for 4.0

known_risks: SPIKE (PR #229) ran Ruby 4.0.9 + Trixie + Node 26 directly on today's main (Rails 7.0.10): after moving pg, byebug, pry, minitest and nokogiri the full suite was green on arm64 (366 examples, 0 failures), assets precompiled and the app booted. The blockers are structural, not runtime: Rails 7.0 is unsupported upstream on 4.0 (8.0.4.1+/8.1.3+ carry the fixes), rubocop 1.28 rejects TargetRubyVersion above 3.2, and CI's base image must be rebuilt first

Only 8 chilled-string warnings appeared, all from shoulda-matchers 5.3 (moved in Phase 10); haml 5.2.2 and coffee-script 2.4.1 emitted none, so Phase 17 is ordering hygiene rather than a hard prerequisite

byebug 13 compiles and runs on 4.0.9 (the earlier `debug` fallback note was unnecessary); RubyGems 4 prints an 'ambiguous specs: reline' warning per run because byebug 13 and Ruby's bundled reline both provide it

Bundler 4's CHECKSUMS section does not appear on an upgraded lockfile, so the first `bundle install` rewrite is small (33 lines in the spike); do it on the arm64 Mac and in CI (x86_64) and confirm the two agree before tagging the base image
Ruby 4.0 stable patch releases ship every two months — pin the full patch version in the FROM line as the repo already does

phases.name: PostgreSQL 16 → 18 (docker-compose + RDS)
phases.rationale: PostgreSQL 16 is supported until 2028-11-09, so this is not urgent, but 18 (2025-09-25, EOL 2030-11-14) is the newest line RDS offers today (RDS announced 18.x minors through 18.6 in August 2026) and 19 (community GA planned 2026-11-19) will take months to reach RDS. Depends on Phase 7 because pg 1.7 is the client built against the newer libpq — Phase 7 merged 2026-10-25, so this is unblocked and can run beside Track B. The app side is a one-line docker-compose change; the real work is the RDS major-version upgrade in core-iac (db_engine_version 16.13 in all three terraform.tfvars) and its test plan. Split into two PRs in two repos so the app-repo half can land any time.

changes.19a_app_repo: docker-compose.yml postgres:16-alpine → postgres:18-alpine (dev + CI); docker-compose.dev.yml's jbergknoff/postgresql-client:latest is an unpinned psql — an older psql against an 18 server only warns about version skew, but pin or replace it if `./go db dev` misbehaves. pg 1.7.0 already bundles libpq 18.6, so client and server will match
changes.19b_core_iac: terraform/env/*/cluster-addons-layer/terraform.tfvars db_engine_version 16.13 → 18.x, development → staging → production, each with a pre-upgrade snapshot; the RDS parameter group family moves from postgres16 to postgres18 in the same change
changes.postgresql_19: Docker Hub already has 19rc1-alpine (2026-10); re-evaluate in 2027 H1 once RDS publishes a GA 19.x; the compose image can move to 19-alpine as soon as the community release lands, but keep compose at most one major ahead of RDS

known_risks: RDS in-place major upgrades 16 → 18 are supported directly; `pg_upgrade` rewrites system catalogs and requires a maintenance window — this app has a single small database, so expect minutes, but take the snapshot
PostgreSQL 17 changed `pg_dump` defaults and 18 changes the default for data checksums and some planner behaviour; schema.rb-driven test DB creation is unaffected
The PostgreSQL major on the dev compose image and on RDS do not have to match, but keeping them one apart at most avoids surprises in `db/schema.rb` generation

Phase 11 waits for Phase 10's lint tooling. Everything from 13 onward is strictly sequential. As of 2026-10-25 Track A is merged except Phase 10 (PR #227, CI green); Track F's Phase 19 is unblocked because Phase 7 merged, so 19a (compose) and 19b (RDS, core-iac) can run beside Track B.
